highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
body: As an AI-powered answer engine, Perplexity is deeply focused on search and accuracy. Its ability to process large amounts of information is critically important. Johnny Ho, Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, observes that every time the model gets better at writing code, Perplexity’s search engine improves too. It becomes able to write better programs that search the web and internal information and summarize it very concisely.
But the real challenge, according to Johnny, is taking those informational aspects and applying them to real-world systems. Something made easier with GPT‑6 Astra.
For Johnny, one of the most useful applications of AI is testing code. With limited time to test manually, he asks GPT‑6 Astra to build a small testing program around an application.

The model generates realistic responses like those another service would send, for example, a language model API or a connector. By standing in for those services, the model can check how the application responds and test the workflow from start to finish.

highlights.title: 5 Near-Perfect Action Shows That Are Streaming Online for Free
highlights.summary: Unfortunately, all of the aforementioned shows require a paid subscription if you wish to enjoy them. If you’re on the lookout for action titles that can be streamed for free on Pluto TV, Tubi, or Roku, look no further.
body: A good action show can turn anyone’s day around. Kinetic choreography in a series like Reacher or Daredevil informs the motivations of its characters while injecting excitement between quieter moments. Some stories even push the limits of what action looks like on television, like Prime Video’s The Boys, which approaches the superhero genre through a viscerally satirical lens.

Sam Raimi’s Evil Dead trilogy puts Ash Williams (Bruce Campbell) through the wringer. Just when you think his trials are over, Ash vs Evil Dead forces an older Ash to combat Deadites 30 years after the ending of Army of Darkness. This time, however, Ash isn’t alone, as sidekicks Pablo (Ray Santiago) and Kelly (Dana DeLorenzo) join his cause. Although Ash is initially reluctant to let go of the peace that came with decades of mundanity, he must take accountability after accidentally unleashing a Deadite plague after reading passages from the Book of the Dead to impress a woman.

highlights.title: ‘Look Back’ Breakouts Furi Nanase and Rokka Okada on Growing Up on a Hirokazu Koreeda Set
highlights.summary: In the coming-of-age drama, the 12-year-old co-stars play aspiring manga artists whose rivalry blossoms into a defining friendship, brought to life via the director’s famously intuitive way with child actors.
body: Like the characters they would ultimately play, child actors Furi Nanase and Rokka Okada could easily have become rivals when they first arrived on the set of Japanese auteur Hirokazu Koreeda ‘s latest acclaimed drama, Look Back. Both 11-year-old fifth graders when filming began, the two actresses came to the film with opposite levels of experience and very different dispositions.

“I remember looking at her on the first day and thinking, Hmm, is she really so good?” says Nanase. “But then we were introduced and started talking, and I was like, wow, this girl is really interesting!”

The pair, who later shared their 12th birthdays on set just one day apart, became instant best buds. By the time of Look Back ‘s well-received world premiere in Venice last week, they had grown inseparable. As a duo, they landed on various fashion outlets’ best-dressed-of-the-festival lists, thanks to their stylishly retro outfits and adorable antics on the red carpet, where they struck coordinated poses and jumped in the air in unison.
The Hollywood Reporter caught up with Nanase and Okada on the Lido the following day for what amounted to their very first interview with the international press.

highlights.title: A taste of home: discovering Sweden’s local food heroes
highlights.summary: Chefs in the east of the country are shunning imported produce for local ingredients, reinforcing how food is intertwined with a region and its people. ‘It’s a magical place, and not just because of the hotel.” Standing outside the greenhouses at Högbo Brukshotell, two hours north of Stockholm…
body: The catalyst was disarmingly simple. Years ago, a journalist asked Johansson why he was cooking the food he was cooking. Like many ambitious Swedish chefs, Stefan trained in Stockholm’s top restaurants, where ingredients from around the world were only a phone call away. The question lingered long after the interview ended.

“Before, I wanted food to be spectacular; I didn’t really care where it came from,” he says. “Then I closed the window of where we source from down to the region. It was the best thing I’ve ever done.” Instead of looking farther afield for inspiration, he began looking closer to home.

Högbo Brukshotell sits in the former Högbo ironworks, a quiet pocket of forest, waterways and historic buildings north of Sandviken. The area’s industrial past is still visible in its old manor houses, smithies and mill buildings, but since the factories fell silent in the mid-19th century, the woods have reclaimed their place. Walking, cycling and cross-country ski trails now lead into the forest, while the old bruk buildings house cafes, workshops and small businesses.

highlights.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
highlights.summary: It comes as the AI firm's boss has called for the technology's development to be slowed down, citing "serious" risks.
body: An artificial intelligence researcher who quit AI firm Anthropic has said people working on the technology were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.
Jacob Coxon told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg on Saturday about his viral resignation post in which he raised concerns about out-of-control AI.
"I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," he said.
His resignation comes amid growing safety concerns in the industry, including from his former boss, Anthropic head Dario Amodei, who in an essay argued for development to slow down.

highlights.title: Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AI
highlights.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says the time has come to slow down AI development and will give third-party evaluators like METR access to its models to help ensure its "adherence to safety practices and commitments." In a winding essay, Amodei proposed a three-step plan to "pace the frontier" - jargon…
body: Dario Amodei proposed a three-step plan to ‘pace the frontier’ of AI development.

Amodei says that giving external evaluators wide-ranging access is just the first step, and one it is taking now unilaterally. Step two would involve the industry coming together as a whole, likely with government agencies to “establish common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” This step would focus on AI companies operating in democratic countries, but because passing laws and building regulatory infrastructure takes time, Amodei says that the industry should work together to create safety standards.

The third step would be the most challenging — getting authoritarian governments like those in China and Russia to agree to slow development and adopt a global set of AI safety standards. But he also says it’s crucial that the US and other democracies maintain a technological lead over China and other authoritarian regimes by limiting their access to high-powered chips and cracking down on things like distillation that allow companies to quickly catch up by training its AI to replicate the behavior of a more powerful model.

highlights.title: Prime Video's Reacher Is Officially Returning Next Month After a Stellar Season 4
highlights.summary: If there’s one thing Reacher fans can count on, it’s that Jack Reacher is never gone for very long. The Prime Video series has turned Lee Child’s wandering ex-military cop into one of TV ’s most reliably entertaining action heroes.
body: Not quite. Jack Reacher is already slated for a return this October, just not on television. Lee and Andrew Child are releasing a new novel in the exciting series called Chain Reaction, the 31st Jack Reacher outing, giving fans another dose of the beloved character before the show returns for its fifth season.

If Alan Ritchson ’s portrayal of the character has become one of your biggest TV obsessions, there’s never been a better moment to dive into the books. While the show does a fantastic job of introducing Lee Child’s iconic character — even better than the Tom Cruise movies — more than three decades of stories are waiting on the page. Child’s prose delivers a brand of pulse-pounding satisfaction for mystery buffs that the screen can only begin to match, and his latest offering is slated to be another exciting thrill ride.

highlights.summary: International sales company Parallax Films has boarded “Aman,” writer-director Rahul Roye’s short film about a trans man who discovers he is pregnant on the eve of his gender-affirming surgery, for worldwide sales.
body: Parallax founder Liuying Cao said: “‘Aman’ is an ambitious film, yet one deeply grounded in human emotion. It touches upon the most intimate experiences of an individual life, while never losing sight of the social and political realities – and responsibilities – that those experiences carry. Rather than resorting to slogans, the film reaches the audience through pain that is visceral, embodied, and deeply human. We are especially thrilled to be collaborating with such a beautiful and moving queer film from India.”

The 16-minute film, a U.K.-U.S.-India-France co-production shot in the Hindi and Bengali languages, had previously unveiled Nikkhil Advani and Dominique Welinski as executive producers. It is produced by Apoorva Bakshi for Awedacious Originals, Elle León Nostas for Aymara Films, Neeraj Churi for Lotus Visual Productions, and Tushar Tyagi and Abid Aziz Merchant.

highlights.title: Rise of the student commuters: weighing the costs of living at home or in halls
highlights.summary: Changing social trends and creative timetables are making it more likely for students to stay at home while they study. Is campus life on the way out? For Lucy Brazier, a second-year business management student, commuting to university was an easy decision.
body: And with overnight accommodation available on campus, she feels she gets the best of both worlds. “I can book a room at less than a day’s notice for £35 so I don’t have to drive home. I’ve used it after nights out, and the evening before exams so I don’t have the stress of driving in the morning. It’s been really helpful.”
Brazier is far from alone. More students are choosing to live at home while studying, and universities are increasingly adapting their courses and campuses to make commuting easier.

According to Ucas, 612,690 UK students aged 18 to 20 who applied before 14 January 2026 made at least one application stating that they intended to live at home – up 8% from last year’s figure of 569,880.

With commuter students now a significant presence on campus, Universities UK chief executive Vivienne Stern says the traditional model of student life is changing. “Universities are evolving to meet the needs of learners. Many offer flexible ways to access learning and resources, or adjust students’ timetables to suit those with longer commutes or other responsibilities.”

highlights.title: Trump is giving data centers a pass to pollute
highlights.summary: President Donald Trump is weakening environmental regulations in the name of speeding up the construction of AI data centers, raising health risks for Americans, a cadre of former EPA officials said this week in a briefing and new report.
body: The Trump administration is sacrificing Americans’ health to build data centers, former EPA officials warn.

At the start of his term, Trump’s EPA administrator, Lee Zeldin, proclaimed his goal of making America “ the AI capital of the world ” through deregulation. Since then, Zeldin and the White House have rolled back dozens of rules on top of cutting staff and funding at the US EPA.

As a result of the Trump administration’s deregulation spree and attacks on renewable energy, the wave of new AI data centers is increasingly powered by dirty energy that can impact Americans’ health even if they don’t live near a data center, the group of EPA alumni warn. They say that the agency they once worked for, which was created to “ protect human health and the environment,” is no longer the watchdog it should be as the physical infrastructure underpinning generative AI changes America’s landscape.
“You would think that an industry buildout of this magnitude, billed as a revolution, would mean more vigilance from EPA.”

highlights.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
highlights.summary: Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.
body: The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

Arsenal had to withstand late pressure from the home side, with Raya saving well from Nordi Mukiele, but they made the result safe when Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty after Reinildo Mandava was shown a second yellow card for hauling him down.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Is About to Totally Reinvent One of the Best Experiences in Video Games
highlights.summary: It’s quite literally the name of the game: Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto series is all about stealing cars. And the latest installment of the franchise, GTA 6, seems like it’s about to revolutionize one of the most thrilling experiences players can have in a video game.
body: Back in GTA 5, stealing cars was a more streamlined affair: you’d approach a vehicle with someone in it, and force them out with a single button press. You could also aim your weapon at them to force them to abandon the car, or bust open the window of a parked car with a well-placed elbow, but it was still a pretty simple process. That’s no longer the case in GTA 6.

According to IGN, the latest game in the series will introduce a tiered security system for stealing cars. Just like in real life, pricier vehicles with enhanced technology will require specific skills and tools to steal. That means players will have to think more deeply about which cars to boost, and when. This time around, Jason and Lucia will have access to a device called a “wank scanner,” which will display information about a car’s security system and value.

What’s more, unlike in previous GTA games, in GTA 6, you’ll be able to sell any car you’ve stolen. This game will have a fence system for stolen goods that’s more similar to that of 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2. Who doesn’t appreciate a lucrative side-hustle?

highlights.summary: Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana” has been chosen as the official entry from the Philippines in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. It was selected from a shortlist of 8 films. The film is written and directed by Manuel and is distributed by Kino Lorber.
body: Rafael Manuel ’s “ Filipiñana ” has been chosen as the official entry from the Philippines in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. It was selected from a shortlist of 8 films.

Speaking with Variety, Manuel said he felt the golf course was the perfect setting for the film to explore societal inequities in the country. With the very first courses established on American military bases, the local elite eventually took over, making the golf course a center of power.

“When you think about it, it’s a good metaphor for the country in that it’s very large and situated on a very fertile plot of land that’s toiled on and worked on by so many people, but ultimately enjoyed and profited from by only a select few.” That, Manuel said, illustrates the class divide that has been so ingrained in the Philippines.

highlights.title: My partner’s sister has published a family memoir that's unfair to him. Should we cut ties? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
highlights.summary: She should have been much more careful, but everyone has their own version of the ‘truth’. Does your partner want a reconciliation? My sister-in-law wrote and published an emotionally charged “memoir” of family dislocation and trauma, in which she massaged the truth of her family’s past to portray…
body: She tried to de‑identify her brother, but he would be recognisable to anyone with a rudimentary ability to search the internet. Legal action was considered, but decided against. Who gets to tell a story in these times? Whose story is more “true ”? And should we cut off all ties or attempt reconciliation?

You have every right to be aggrieved. This sounds upsetting, unfair and also largely avoidable. Unless your partner’s inclusion was an essential and pivotal part of the book (in which case he may have wanted to write the story himself), I wonder why he was included in a way that could identify him, and why she didn’t give you a heads-up.

But family members don’t always behave in ways we like, and in families there is usually one person who feels they own the narrative and know all the truths. It may feel as if, by putting her account in a book, your sister-in-law has claimed the definitive, “true” version. But that’s just her side of it. Your question about “who gets to tell a story” is pertinent because not everyone will go on to write a memoir, but many people can and do post a mini version on social media.
points: She should have been much more careful, but everyone has their own version of the ‘truth’.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says it would be ‘ill-advised’ to go public in 2026
highlights.summary: While OpenAI has filed confidentially for an IPO, the company will not be going public this year, according to CEO Sam Altman.
body: Altman was interviewed recently by Fortune editor in chief Alyson Shontell; amidst the fallout from the OpenAI-HuggingFace hack, as well as broader discussions about AI safety, Shontell asked whether OpenAI still feels pressure to “move really fast” due to its IPO plans.
“We’re not rushing into an IPO,” Altman said. “I actually think that given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public.”

Instead, he insisted that OpenAI will go public “when we’re ready, which is when the business is ready, when we feel ready from what the moment is like in society with this technology.” When pressed on whether that means the IPO isn’t happening in 2026, Altman replied, “I would say not 2026, yeah. We’ve got a lot of stuff to do.”

The New York Times reported in June that although OpenAI had hired bankers and lawyers with the goal of going public in the third or fourth quarter of 2026, the company was leaning toward 2027 due to the volatility of tech stocks and its own financial challenges.

highlights.title: The AfD won a shock election in Germany. Elon Musk was thrilled
highlights.summary: The billionaire and the party have developed a symbiotic relationship to spread their far-right views both in Germany and the US. The Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party rattled European politics this week after a convincing victory in a German state election, which placed it only a few seats…
body: “Gut gemacht!” Musk posted on X a week ago, using the German phrase for “well done” as he congratulated AfD party leader, Alice Weidel. It was one of at least a dozen posts the Tesla and SpaceX CEO made about the AfD following the result.

The AfD reciprocated Musk’s praise, with the party’s Saxony-Anhalt leader, Ulrich Siegmund, thanking the tech mogul for his support. Siegmund, who wants German schools to focus less on responsibility for the second world war and whose top staffers include four former members of a banned neo-Nazi youth group, called Musk a “visionary”.

Musk has become a central figure in the global far-right in recent years, using his support and influence to back anti-immigrant activists, illiberal leaders and nativist parties. Along with a preoccupation with race in the UK, much of that attention has been focused on the AfD, and the major results in the Saxony-Anhalt election, and Musk’s jubilation at their win, have revived scrutiny of his connections to it.

highlights.title: 35 Years Later, the Greatest Detective Thriller Series of All Time Is Officially Free on Streaming
highlights.summary: Fall makes for a great setting. There’s something special about the thick foliage and heavy clouds as the backdrop for a mercurial town, especially when a story is set within the framework of genre.
body: No show did this with more originality than Twin Peaks. Developed by David Lynch and Mark Frost, Twin Peaks is about a murder investigation, at least on paper. While it only ran for two seasons on ABC in the ‘90s, the series proved to be so much more than its premise suggested thanks largely to Lynch’s mood-first style of storytelling. In 2017, he returned to the world he helped establish with Twin Peaks: The Return – completing his vision and cementing the series as a must-watch for cinephiles, regardless of genre preferences.

Twin Peaks begins with the murder of Laura Palmer (Sheryl Lee), the town’s sweetheart and homecoming queen, whose body is unexpectedly washed ashore, naked and wrapped in plastic. As the town’s residents mourn her loss, FBI Agent Dale Cooper (Kyle MacLachlan) arrives to investigate. But he very quickly begins peeling back seemingly endless layers to a vast mystery involving awful parents, weird psychologists, and an evil supernatural force. With each episode, the town’s secrets deepen, and the show expands in scope, exploring all manner of characters and stories, from cheating teens to money laundering and trafficking schemes.

highlights.title: Ketchup on a Sunday roast? This is the worst thing gen Z has ever done | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: Swapping roast potatoes and yorkshire puddings for kimchi and avocado – how can they live with themselves? Trigger warning: the following contains a description of the most heinous abomination known to humankind. Ready? A diabolical 39% of gen Z add ketchup to their Sunday roast.
body: And their misdemeanours do not end there. In news that is particularly distressing on the eve of glorious roast season, it turns out they’re also exchanging roast potatoes and yorkshire puddings for hot sauce, kimchi and – sounds like a punchline, but isn’t – literally avocado.

Sorry, but how dare they? You do not mess with perfection, which is what a roast is – that’s why so many of us choose it for our imaginary death row last meal. It’s comforting, delicious, a ritual and a treat. Peak food. Never mind the audacity of tweaking it at all – the tweaks themselves add insult to injury. The roast potato is the star of the plate, for goodness sake! Substituting it is like taking Meryl Streep out of a movie, and replacing her with … well, an avocado.

Gen Z are also determined to cut off their noses to spite their faces, with a horrifying 14% of them eschewing gravy. This is clearly a travesty. Leaving your roast dry is not allowing it to achieve its full potential, cheating it of fulfilling its destiny. How can they live with themselves?

highlights.title: Anthropic CEO outlines plan to slow AI development
highlights.summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman seem to agree that it's time to "pace the frontier." What would that actually look like?
body: We’ve been seeing increasingly dire warnings from AI researchers about the dangers of artificial intelligence, and even comments from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that it may be time to “pace” AI development. But what would that actually look like?

In a new blog post, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei not only echoed the call to “pace the frontier,” but also outlined three broad strategies for doing so. And he said Anthropic is “unilaterally committing” to one of them, with Altman chiming in to say OpenAI will follow suit.

The debate over AI safety and alignment intensified this week after researcher Jacob Coxon wrote that he’s resigning from Anthropic over concerns that the leading AI companies are “gambling with our lives” while the people building the technology “earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” a claim repeated by others at Anthropic.
points: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman seem to agree that it's time to "pace the frontier.

highlights.title: ‘Cheap iPhone deal’: warning over scam sites selling latest Apple mobiles
highlights.summary: Criminals exploit demand for iPhone 18 Pro and foldable Duo to trick people eager to get their hands on one. Apple has just launched a range of new iPhones, including a foldable handset, just as you decide it is time to replace your own ageing mobile.
body: Searching online for a better price with the words “cheap”, “iPhone” and “deal”, you come across a website which offers an iPhone 18 Pro for a couple of hundred pounds less than the Apple site. You pay for the new phone via a bank transfer and wait for it to arrive.

But the website is a fraud - one of hundreds set up in the days before the new Apple phones were announced – and is designed to scam money out of people eager to get their hands on one of the new handsets.
Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable phone, on Wednesday, as well as two new iPhone 18 Pro models.

At the same time, criminals were building up networks of fake sites. Security researchers found a large spike in the number of scam sites registered with “Apple” and “iPhone”, among other keywords, in their domain names.

The characters around her go quiet, and the crowd at the Toronto International Film Festival, where Chris Rock’s film made its world premiere…
body: “It was such a raw and honest take on the darker side of our industry,” Eleazar said about reading the script for the first time (and charming the crowd with her British accent). “She’s such a complex and such a contradictory and flawed character, and I’m sort of drawn to characters that are difficult to love, and the way that Chris wrote the individual relationships with such precision and nuance.”

“The moment I read the script in London, I was desperate to do this part. So I did whatever I could,” Eleazar said, before realizing what she’d accidentally insinuated, since Misty Green will indeed do anything for a role. Rock and the crowd chuckled as she hastily recovered: “Normal things! Just like Zooms and stuff.”

Eleazar — recently named one of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch for 2026 — is a best actress contender that dares anyone in the room to argue otherwise. Each scene feels fit for her Oscar clip package, much Cate Blanchett delivered in each beat of “Blue Jasmine.” Misty is a fading, award-winning actress clawing back her career, but self-sabotaging along the way. Eleazar plays her with the danger of Pam Grier and the polish of Tracee Ellis Ross.

highlights.summary: Plus: The US disrupts the internet’s biggest black market, a Conti ransomware hacker gets prison time, Meta fails to stop AI-generated videos of child abuse.
body: Editor’s note: After more than a decade, this is the last WIRED Security News This Week. “The roundup,” as we call it internally, started as a way to ensure that our readers knew about the latest key cybersecurity and privacy news even if we didn’t write about it ourselves. It was a simple way to highlight our own work and the wealth of other great journalism and research published in this realm every week.

Over the years, the roundup has developed a devoted following, and some editions have even become viral hits—which is honestly weird, but the cybersecurity community is great and weird, so it feels right. Rest assured that something new and exciting is coming in the roundup’s place, so stay tuned for that! For now, as always, stay safe out there.

Meta failed to catch roughly 350 AI child abuse ads, according to new research this week, including some that included images of real kids. In one case, a child depicted in an ad was a member of a European royal family. Lawmakers have said they intend to investigate, and the San Francisco City Attorney’s Office ordered the company this week to stop “allowing” AI child abuse ads.

body: StarCraft is finally getting a new game, and it’s taking a drastically different approach from its predecessors; instead of an RTS, Blizzard’s grisly sci-fi property is making its debut in the realm of open-world shooters, and it’s set to launch in 2030.

That’s a long way out from now, and it’s anyone’s guess as to what the world will look like in four years. We got the chance to ask the developers everyone’s burning question at Blizzcon 2026: Why announce the game if there’s still so much time left before it releases?
Dan Hay, GM & VP of StarCraft and AnaLee Haertling, Associate Director, told us that sharing a firm release date helps keep them “honest” — and yes, 2030 is a firm release date.
When asked if 2030 was a solid date, Hay confirmed that it is, indeed, “solid.”

highlights.title: Elena Rybakina Wins the US Open Women’s Championship
highlights.summary: Elena Rybakina is the freshly crowned US Open women’s champion, beating Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in a closely fought match on Saturday.
body: It’s Rybakina’s third major, having won Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.

It’s Rybakina who came out of the gate faster, stronger, and with fewer errors—serving hard and with pinpoint accuracy, and seemingly bloodless in her power and precision on her way to taking the first set 6-4 (hence her sometime nickname on tour, the “Ice Queen”). Sabalenka’s composure, meanwhile, was maybe best expressed by the warning she received early in the first set for ball abuse after sending one high into the crowd in a moment of frustration.

The two had faced each other 17 times before on the tour, with Sabalenka winning 10 of those matches—but they’d been dead even since 2023. Perhaps more crucially, they’d played each other in two Grand Slam finals (both at the Australian Open), with each player winning once.

body: LG has responded to our deep-dive investigation revealing the depths of LG Smart TV ACR data harvesting functionality, LG's claims to "owning the glass," and LG Smart TV security vulnerabilities and exploits. When LG responded to GamersNexus, it called our report untrue and, essentially, claimed the "fake news" defense. We believe the company failed to present a single point of evidence to counter our findings. In this video, we dismantle LG's response and bring in lawyer Vincent Agosta to analyze their terms so that consumers understand what they're agreeing to.
